question: In distributed database systems, what does the CAP theorem state regarding Consistency (C), Availability (A), and Partition tolerance (P)?
choices: A distributed system can guarantee at most two of the three properties simultaneously in the presence of network partitions
All three properties can be guaranteed concurrently under standard network conditions
Only Consistency can be guaranteed across distributed nodes
Partition tolerance can be eliminated by increasing server bandwidth
answer: A distributed system can guarantee at most two of the three properties simultaneously in the presence of network partitions
explanation: Eric Brewer's CAP theorem establishes that in any asynchronous distributed network subject to partitions, a system cannot simultaneously guarantee both consistency and availability.

question: What is the primary objective of database sharding (horizontal partitioning)?
choices: Distributing subsets of table rows across multiple servers to improve scalability and throughput
Splitting columns of a table into separate vertical tables
Backing up transaction logs to cold storage
Normalizing data into Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF)
answer: Distributing subsets of table rows across multiple servers to improve scalability and throughput
explanation: Sharding distributes rows of a table across multiple database nodes, enabling horizontal scaling to support large-scale workloads and massive datasets.
